title: Construction of a high-NFOM multiphoton microscope with large-angle resonant raster scanning
protocol: Optically couple pulsed laser output to the resonant scanning mirror.
Expand the laser output to fulfill the clear aperture requirement of the resonant scanning mirror.
Couple the resonant scanning mirror to the galvanometer scanning mirror.
Maintain a separation of approximately 12.5 mm between the centers of the resonant and galvanometer scanning mirrors.
Optically couple the galvanometer scanning mirror to the general scan lens LSM05-BB.
Ensure a distance of 66 mm from the galvanometer mirror to the front surface of LSM05-BB.
Optically couple LSM05-BB to the custom tube lens unit.
Separate the last surface of LSM05-BB from the front surface of the custom tube lens by 261 mm.
Build the custom tube lens using three plano-convex lenses (Edmund Optics: 86-925).
Combine the three lenses with minimal separation to prevent surface damage.
Mount the lenses in series using three adjustable ring mounts, such as Edmund Optics model 03-670.
Ensure the height of the three mounts is maintained at the same level and are parallel to each other.
Optically couple the custom tube lens to XLUMPlanFl, 20×/0.95W objective lens.
Separate the last surface of the custom tube lens unit from the back aperture of the objective lens by 172 mm.
Place appropriate band pass filter(s) prior to the photosensitive area of the PMT to ensure detection of the specific signal of interest.
Use FF01-580/60-25-D, Semrock to ensure detection of Nav1.8-tdTomato or Alexa Fluor 546 two-photon fluorescence signals.
Use an additional color glass filter in series (FGB37-A, Thorlabs) to reject any residual reflection of the excitation wavelength.
Make sure the computer is powered off.
Install the PCIe-6341 multifunction I/O card in an ×4 or higher bandwidth PCIe slot.
Install the ATS9440 digitizer in an ×8 or higher bandwidth PCIe slot.
Install the Quadro RTX 8000 graphics card in an ×16 PCIe slot.
Connect CRS 4 kHz to its respective driver board.
Ensure a stable power supply for the CRS 4 kHz driver.
Connect the laser pulse sync signal from Fidelity 2 to the external clock input of ATS9440.
Feed the electrical signal from R10699 to C6438-01.
Connect the amplified output from C6438-01 to channel A of ATS9440.
Feed the line trigger sync signal from CRS 4 kHz driver to a voltage buffer (50LD, Thorlabs).
Split the output from the voltage buffer into Sync-A and Sync-B using ZFRSC-42-S+.
Connect Sync-A to the external trigger input of ATS9440.
Connect Sync-B to PFI14 of PCIe-6341.
Connect the amplitude control pin of the CRS 4 kHz driver to AO 0 pin of PCIe-6341.
Insert 6757 DAC into MicroMax 671 driver.
Plug one end of the ribbon cable to 6757 DAC according to cable indications.
Plug the other end of the ribbon cable to digital I/O pins on PCIe-6341.
Connect DB0-DB15 pins of 6757 sequentially to P0.0-P0.7 and P1.0-P1.7 pins of PCIe-6341.
Connect CLR, R/W, CS, and LDAC of 6757 sequentially to P2.0-P2.3 pins of PCIe-6341.
Connect all ground pins of 6757 to the digital ground of PCIe-6341.
Connect TSDM40-15X unit to SHOT-304GS.
Connect SGSP80-20ZF unit (or alternative from Sigma Koki) to SHOT-304GS for axial sample displacement.
Attach two units of TSDM40-15X for sample displacement along horizontal and vertical directions.
Ensure axes of motion of TSDM40-15X units are perpendicular to each other.
Connect combined TSDM40-15X unit to the moving plate of SGSP80-20ZF unit.
Use a typical sample holder, such as MPSH or MPSHSS from Thorlabs, for holding a specimen.
Connect R10699 to C9525 using a good-quality HSV cable.
Connect SHOT-304GS and C9525 to the computer through USB cables.
Feed the output of R10699 to C6438-01.
Amplify the output of C6438-01 and feed it to Channel A of ATS9440.
Optionally, use 50LD or other alternatives if line trigger signal from CRS driver is high impedance.
Optional: Employ a phase matching circuit to fine-tune sampling events with laser-pulses for optimal signal collection.
Obtain the SetUp LASERaster+.exe file from the lead contact.
Run SetUp LASERaster+.exe.
Install .NET framework (version 4.6.1 or newer).
Install NVIDIA driver (version 30.0.0 or newer).
Install Alazar card driver (version 6.7.0 or newer).
If NI-DAQmx is newer than version 18.6, install the NI package manager first.
Check "NI-DAQmx Support for C" during the installation process of the NI package manager.
Install NIDAQmx runtime (version 18.6.0 or newer).
Enter Resonant Scanner Settings.
Measure the actual frequency of your resonant scanner using an oscilloscope and enter the value in kHz unit.
Keep the default Sync Signal Trigger Voltage setting.
Align a visible laser to the resonating mirror and let the reflected beam fall on a wall.
Calculate the optical angle (θ) as θ = 2 tan⁻¹(0.5d/D).
Gradually increase RS-angle and note down the RS voltage for each step in Real time info panel.
Plot voltage vs optical angle as shown in Figure 6C.
Enter the linear-fitted slope and intercept obtained from the plot.
Enable Alignment mode on Main Control Panel → Align.
Enter Galvo Scanner Settings.
Align the visible laser to the galvanometer mirror and let the reflected beam fall on a wall.
Set Galvo step to 0 in Alignment mode and mark the laser spot position.
Mark a second position for the 65535th step.
Calculate the angle and enter the same.
Change PCIe device number to DEV 2, DEV 3, or other if software control fails.
Enter Additional Settings.
Enter external clock frequency with your laser repetition rate in MHz unit.
Confirm exact value with an oscilloscope.
Enter axis numbers for axial, horizontal, and vertical linear stages under 3D Stage Settings.
Check Invert option if a stage needs to move in the opposite direction.
Specify COM port of C9525 unit under PMT HV Supply.
Change Default Storage Drive under Storage Settings to one with fast read/write capability (recommended: PCIe SSD).
Click Apply to save settings.
Click Configure and then Start on Main Control Panel.
Refer to Data Saving Panel and start saving data in binary format.
Check Activate Viewer on Data Read Panel.
Click Load, navigate, and select your data location on Data Read Panel.
Select frames to export from Batch Export Settings.
Click Export and select a destination directory.
Set Slice #, Z step (μm), and axial motion direction (UP/DW) while acquiring an imaging stack at a specific lateral (XY) position in Data Saving Panel.
Image a standard test target along both horizontal and vertical directions for FOV calibration.
Ensure a low average excitation power to reduce damage to the target during imaging.
Export a horizontal image of the stage micrometer with disabled Calibrate Images and Fix Distortion in Batch Export Panel.
Enter the X-pixel coordinate of each vertical line from both left and right halves of the image sequentially.
Check Batch Input to paste all values at once.
Keep Polynomial Degree and Number of Blocks at default values.
Estimate an initial X-FOV value and click Apply.
Export a horizontal image of the stage micrometer with disabled Calibrate Images but enabled Fix Distortion.
Calculate and enter the X-FOV in millimeters.
Click Apply to save the calibrations.
